How it works GitHub Sign in

Run a fleet of Claude Code sessions. One task per window.

claudefleet turns GitHub issues into parallel coding sessions, each in its own git worktree, on every machine you own, sharing one pool of subscriptions. Every task ends as its own pull request.

What it does

Many sessions, many machines, one place to see them

Issues in, pull requests out

Hand an issue to a worker. It claims it, works in its own worktree, runs the related tests and opens the PR. You answer questions when it asks.

Subscriptions, pooled

New sessions start on whichever Claude or Codex subscription has the most headroom. A full one is skipped until its window resets.

Every machine you have

Macs, Linux boxes, a rented machine when you run out of room. Sessions move between them; you reach any of them over SSH with a 12-hour certificate.

How it works

Three steps to your first fleet session

Install the client

Run curl … /install | sh on the computer you work from.

Sign in with GitHub

fleet login shows a code; confirm it in the browser. Only people on this hub's list get in.

Hand it an issue

fleet spawn 1961 starts a worker on the best machine and subscription, and it lands as a PR.
